ProphecySummary: When Ben-hadad of Syria besieged Samaria with thirty-two kings, a prophet told Ahab that the LORD would deliver that great multitude into his hand that very day, and that the young men of the princes of the provinces would lead the victory. A year later, when Syria returned saying Israel's God was a god of the hills, another word promised the same deliverance in the plain, so that Syria would know that the LORD is God.
Fulfillment: Both victories happened as spoken: the young men routed the Syrian camp at Samaria, and at Aphek the Israelites defeated a Syrian army, with a wall falling on twenty-seven thousand who remained. Ahab then spared Ben-hadad and made a covenant with him, and a prophet told him his life would answer for Ben-hadad's, a judgment later completed at Ramoth-gilead. The prophet of the first victory is unnamed in the text, so no name is invented for him here.

Prophecy: The Two Witnesses
ProphecySummary: Two witnesses, clothed in sackcloth, will prophesy for 1,260 days with power to shut heaven so it does not rain, turn waters to blood, and strike the earth with plagues as often as they wish. When they have finished their testimony, the beast from the abyss will kill them, their bodies will lie in the street of the great city for three and a half days while the earth rejoices, and then the breath of life from God will enter them and they will stand up and ascend to heaven in a cloud. Their resurrection and ascension will be followed by a great earthquake in which a tenth of the city falls.
Fulfillment: The identity of the two witnesses is debated — Moses and Elijah are commonly suggested because of the plagues and the shutting of heaven, while others read them as symbolic of the witnessing church — and the timing, whether past, future, or both, is likewise debated. The text is clear that their ministry, death, public vindication, and the earthquake that follows are future to John's vision and are meant as a sign that God's testimony cannot finally be silenced. This entry therefore records the prophecy without settling the witnesses' identities.

Prophecy: Tyre's Downfall
ProphecySummary: Isaiah foretold that Tyre, the crowning city whose merchants were princes and whose traffickers were the honourable of the earth, would be laid waste and forgotten for seventy years, as the days of one king. Its ships of Tarshish would howl, its harbour would fall silent, and after seventy years Tyre would return to its hire and trade with all the kingdoms of the earth. The oracle covers both Tyre and its daughter Sidon.
Fulfillment: Tyre was besieged for thirteen years by Nebuchadnezzar, lost its island stronghold to Alexander the Great in 332 BC when he built a causeway to it, and never regained its former imperial glory as a merchant empire. A modern city called Tyre exists on the site, so a literal reading of permanent uninhabitation is not claimed here, and the entry is marked partially fulfilled. Its fall as the crowning merchant power, however, is a matter of history.
RelatedEvents: Nebuchadnezzar's Siege of Tyre; Alexander's Capture of Tyre

Prophecy: The Valley of Vision and Shebna's Fall
ProphecySummary: Isaiah pictured Jerusalem, the valley of vision, in a day of trouble and perplexity, with its people fleeing to the housetops and its valley full of chariots at the gates. In the same oracle the LORD announced that Shebna, steward over the house, would be driven from his station and pulled down, and that Eliakim son of Hilkiah would be given the key of the house of David. The chapter joins a siege picture with a named official's displacement.
Fulfillment: Shebna was indeed displaced, and Eliakim son of Hilkiah appears in his place as steward in the Hezekiah narratives, holding office during Sennacherib's siege. Jerusalem suffered the distress of siege, most terribly in the Babylonian conquest of 586 BC, after the earlier Assyrian siege of 701 BC. Because the siege picture finds echoes in more than one siege, the entry is marked partially fulfilled, with Shebna's fall fulfilled in full.
RelatedEvents: Hezekiah and Sennacherib's Invasion; Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Prophecy: Water in the Valley and Victory Over Moab
ProphecySummary: When the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom marched against rebellious Moab and found no water for their armies, Elisha told them to fill the valley with ditches, promising that they would see neither wind nor rain, yet the valley would be filled with water, and that the LORD would also deliver Moab into their hand.
Fulfillment: Water flowed into the valley at the time of the morning sacrifice, the Moabites mistook the red water for blood and rushed to spoil, and Israel struck them down and ravaged their land. The victory was real but incomplete: when the king of Moab sacrificed his eldest son on the wall, great indignation came upon Israel and they withdrew. The entry is therefore marked Partially Fulfilled, honouring both the water and the victory and the withdrawal that followed.
RelatedPeople: Elisha; Jehoram, King of Israel; King Jehoshaphat; Mesha, King of Moab

Prophecy: Woes on the Unrepentant Cities
ProphecySummary: Jesus pronounced woes on Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum, cities where most of His mighty works had been done yet which had not repented. He said it would be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon, and even for Sodom, in the day of judgment than for those cities. Capernaum, exalted to heaven in privilege, would be brought down to hell for its unbelief.
Fulfillment: Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum faded from prominence after the first century, and Capernaum in particular lies in ruins today, a stark contrast to its honoured place in Jesus's ministry. Their loss of standing matches the judgment of privilege Jesus pronounced, though the final day of judgment He named still lies ahead. The prophecy is therefore partially fulfilled, with its historical decline visible and its final judgment still future.

Prophecy: Wolves After Paul's Departure
ProphecySummary: In his farewell to the Ephesian elders at Miletus, Paul warned that after his departing grievous wolves would enter in among them, not sparing the flock. He added that also of their own selves men would arise, speaking perverse things to draw away disciples after them. He therefore urged them to watch and remember his three years of tearful warning night and day.
Fulfillment: Within the first century the churches faced false teachers and divisive figures, as Paul's own later letters and the letter to Ephesus in Revelation show in testing false apostles. The pattern has continued through church history, with new teachers arising from within as well as from outside. The warning is therefore partially fulfilled, already visible in the apostolic age and still unfolding.

Prophecy: The Woman and the Dragon
ProphecySummary: John saw a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars, crying out in birth pains, and a great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns waiting to devour her child as soon as it was born. The child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron, was caught up to God and to his throne, and the woman fled into the wilderness where God had prepared a place for her to be nourished for 1,260 days. War then broke out in heaven, Michael and his angels fought the dragon, the ancient serpent called the devil and Satan was cast down to the earth, and he pursued the woman and made war with the rest of her offspring who keep God's commandments and hold the testimony of Jesus.
Fulfillment: The woman's identity is debated — Israel, the church, Mary, and Eve's offspring have all been proposed — and the wilderness period and heavenly war are read by some as already accomplished at Christ's birth, ascension, and the church's suffering, and by others as still future. This entry is kept distinct from the covered Seed of the Woman entry, which cites Revelation 12:9 only for the serpent's identity; Revelation 12 as a whole adds the birth, ascension, wilderness nourishment, war in heaven, and persecution of the woman's offspring, which the Genesis entry does not contain. Fulfillment is therefore partial and debated rather than simply settled.
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; The Ascension; Great Tribulation

Prophecy: The Worthless Shepherd
ProphecySummary: After the true shepherd was rejected and valued at thirty pieces of silver, Zechariah was told to take the implements of a foolish shepherd, for God will raise up a shepherd in the land who will not visit the cut off, seek the young, heal the broken, or feed the standing, but will eat the flesh of the fat and tear their claws. Woe is then pronounced on the idol shepherd who leaves the flock: the sword will be upon his arm and his right eye, his arm will be clean dried up, and his right eye utterly darkened.
Fulfillment: The identity of this shepherd is debated, and no consensus identification with a single historical ruler has been established: proposals have included bad rulers in the intertestamental period, Roman oppressors, and a future oppressive ruler or antichrist figure. Because the referent is debated, and the judgment on the shepherd has no agreed dated fulfillment, this entry is marked Debated, with the text's own warning about exploitative shepherds stated plainly and no identification asserted as certain.

Prophecy: The Writing on the Wall: The Fall of Babylon
ProphecySummary: At Belshazzar's feast, a hand wrote MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN on the palace wall, and Daniel explained that God had numbered Belshazzar's kingdom and finished it. The king had been weighed in the balances and found wanting, and his kingdom would be divided and given to the Medes and Persians. That same night the prophecy pointed to the end of Babylonian rule.
Fulfillment: Daniel 5 reports that Belshazzar was slain that very night, and Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians under Cyrus in 539 BC. The sudden fall of the Babylonian kingdom matches the writing's warning that the kingdom was finished and divided. This entry is marked Fulfilled on the strength of the biblical account and the historically attested fall of Babylon in 539 BC.

Prophecy: Zerubbabel the Signet Ring
ProphecySummary: On the same day Haggai spoke of shaking heaven and earth and overthrowing the thrones of kingdoms, God told Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, that He will take him as His servant and make him as a signet ring. A signet was the king's personal seal of authority, so the promise marked Zerubbabel as chosen and treasured by God in a time when Judah had no king of its own. The oracle is set in the shaking of the nations, when the kingdoms of the heathen would be broken and their armies fall by each other's swords.
Fulfillment: Zerubbabel did complete the Second Temple, but no record shows him crowned as king or overthrowing empires in his lifetime, and he disappears from history after the temple's completion, so a literal royal fulfillment in his own person is not documented. The promise is therefore debated: some read it as God's preservation and honouring of Zerubbabel himself, while others read the signet as pointing through his line, which Matthew's genealogy traces to Jesus, to the true Davidic King. Because the referent is debated, this entry is marked Debated, not as a settled fulfillment.
RelatedEvents: Rebuilding of the Temple; Return from Exile

Prophecy: Zion's Remnant Restored
ProphecySummary: After judgment, Zephaniah promised that God will gather the outcasts, save her that halteth, and turn their captivity before their eyes. The LORD will take away judgments, cast out the enemy, and rejoice over Zion with joy, singing, and quiet love, while the meek remnant will trust in His name and no longer do iniquity. The daughter of Zion is told to sing and shout, for the King of Israel is in her midst and she shall not see evil any more.
Fulfillment: A remnant returned from Babylon and rebuilt Jerusalem, so the gathering and the turning of captivity began in history, and Christians read the rejoicing King in the midst as fulfilled in Christ dwelling among His people. Zion has not yet known the complete end of shame and evil that Zephaniah pictures, with all nations gathered and the dispersed fully restored. The promise is therefore partly fulfilled, begun in return and in Christ, and awaiting its final joy.
RelatedEvents: Return from Exile; Gathering of the Remnant

Prophecy: Zion's Restoration and the Nations' Homage
ProphecySummary: Isaiah foretold that barren Zion would enlarge her tent, break forth on the right hand and the left, and see her children gather from afar, with the wealth of the nations and kings bringing their glory into her. The sons of strangers would build up her walls, the gates would stand open continually, and her light would draw Gentiles and kings to its brightness. Foreigners and eunuchs who hold fast God's covenant would be given a place in his house and a name better than sons and daughters.
Fulfillment: Jerusalem was rebuilt after the exile, its walls were restored under Nehemiah, and Gentiles did begin to join themselves to the God of Israel, a gathering fulfilled more fully in the Church drawn from all nations. Zion's complete glory, with kings bringing their glory and no more sorrow or oppression, has not yet been seen in full. The prophecy is therefore partially fulfilled, with its historical rebuilding begun and its full glory still to come.
RelatedEvents: Return from Exile; Rebuilding of Jerusalem; The Nations Come to Zion

Prophecy: The One Hundred and Twenty Years
ProphecySummary: Before the Flood, the LORD says his Spirit will not always strive with man, and that man's days will be one hundred and twenty years.
Fulfillment: Debated reading, stated as such: some read the 120 years as the interval before the Flood judgment, others as a new limit on human lifespan. Genesis gives no explicit resolution, and later lifespans in Genesis decline gradually rather than stopping at 120, so neither reading is presented as settled.

Prophecy: Ishmael: A Great Nation, Twelve Princes, a Wild Man
ProphecySummary: The angel of the LORD tells Hagar her seed will be multiplied beyond numbering, that her son Ishmael will be a wild man whose hand is against every man and every man's hand against him, dwelling in the presence of his brethren; God later tells Abraham that Ishmael will beget twelve princes and become a great nation.
Fulfillment: Partly fulfilled in the narrative itself: Genesis 25:13-16 names Ishmael's twelve sons as twelve princes of their tribes, and Genesis 25:17-18 records his descendants dwelling toward Egypt. The 'wild man' description is characterisation of a continuing pattern of conflict rather than a single closed event, so the entry is not marked simply fulfilled.

Prophecy: Sodom and Gomorrah's Destruction Foretold
ProphecySummary: The LORD tells Abraham that the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great and their sin very grievous, and the angels tell Lot that the LORD has sent them to destroy the place.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in Genesis 19:24-25, where the LORD rains brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah and overthrows those cities and the plain.

Prophecy: The Cupbearer Restored and the Baker Hanged in Three Days
ProphecySummary: Joseph interprets the chief butler's dream as restoration to his place within three days, and the chief baker's dream as being hanged within three days, with birds eating his flesh.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled exactly on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday: Genesis 40:20-22 records the butler restored and the baker hanged, as Joseph had interpreted.

Prophecy: Israel Shall Spoil Egypt
ProphecySummary: At the burning bush God says he will give Israel favour in the sight of the Egyptians so that they will not leave empty, but every woman will ask jewels of silver and gold and clothing from her neighbour; Moses later repeats the instruction before the final plague.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in Exodus 12:35-36: Israel asked for jewels of silver and gold and raiment as Moses had said, and the Egyptians gave them, so that Israel spoiled the Egyptians. This entry covers only the spoil detail, not the Exodus itself, which the live four-hundred-years row already covers.

Prophecy: The Ten Plagues Foretold
ProphecySummary: Moses is told to warn Pharaoh that if he refuses to let Israel go, God will slay Egypt's firstborn, and each plague is then announced to Pharaoh before it falls: water turned to blood, frogs, swarms of flies, murrain on cattle, boils, hail, locusts, darkness, and the death of the firstborn, with judgment on Egypt's gods.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled across Exodus 7-12, where each announced plague falls in turn and the firstborn die at midnight in Exodus 12:29, after which Pharaoh lets Israel go. Individual plague announcements are grouped here as one sequence rather than ten separate entries.
KeyPassages: Exodus 4:22-23; Exodus 7:17; Exodus 8:2; Exodus 8:21; Exodus 9:3; Exodus 9:9; Exodus 9:18; Exodus 10:4; Exodus 10:21; Exodus 11:4-5; Exodus 12:12

Prophecy: The Egyptians at the Red Sea Seen No More
ProphecySummary: Standing before the Red Sea, Moses tells Israel not to fear: they will see the LORD's salvation that day, and the Egyptians they have seen that day they will see again no more for ever.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in Exodus 14:27-28, where the sea returns on the Egyptians and covers the chariots and horsemen of Pharaoh's host, so that not so much as one of them remained.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea

Prophecy: Amalek's Remembrance Blotted Out
ProphecySummary: After Israel defeats Amalek at Rephidim, the LORD tells Moses to write as a memorial that he will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven, and that the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
Fulfillment: Partly fulfilled: Amalek is defeated again under Saul (1 Samuel 15) and David, and the last Amalekites are recorded as destroyed in Hezekiah's days (1 Chronicles 4:43), after which Amalek disappears as a distinct people. It is marked partially rather than fully fulfilled because Scripture itself preserves Amalek's name as a warning, so the blotting out is not a single closed event in the text.

Prophecy: The Nations Driven Out Little by Little, Within Promised Borders
ProphecySummary: God promises to send his angel before Israel, to cut off the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites and Jebusites, to send fear before them, and to drive the inhabitants out little by little rather than in one year, setting Israel's bounds from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines and from the desert to the river Euphrates.
Fulfillment: Partly fulfilled: the conquest under Joshua and the judges drives out nations progressively, and the border to the Euphrates is reached under Solomon (1 Kings 4:21), but the land was never held fully and permanently within those bounds, so the promise remains partial in the historical record. Deuteronomy 7:22 restates the little-by-little pattern and is included as a parallel passage, not a separate entry.

Prophecy: Provision in the Sabbatical Year
ProphecySummary: Answering the question of what Israel will eat in the seventh year when they neither sow nor gather, God promises to command his blessing in the sixth year so that it brings forth fruit for three years, covering the seventh year, the eighth year's sowing, and eating of old store until the ninth year's fruit comes in.
Fulfillment: Debated as an event, stated as such: no narrative in Scripture records a specific sixth-year triple harvest, and the promise is conditional on keeping the sabbatical year, which Israel often neglected (the land later enjoying its sabbaths in exile, 2 Chronicles 36:21). The promise is drafted as a genuine predictive provision, but its historical fulfilment cannot be verified from a dated narrative account.

Prophecy: Quail for a Whole Month
ProphecySummary: Moses tells the complaining people they will eat flesh, not for one, two, five, ten or twenty days, but for a whole month until it becomes loathsome to them, because they despised the LORD and wept over leaving Egypt.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in Numbers 11:31-33: a wind from the LORD brings quails from the sea in abundance around the camp, and the people gather them, though a plague follows while the flesh is still between their teeth.

Prophecy: Forty Years of Wandering: That Generation Shall Fall
ProphecySummary: After the spies' unbelief, God declares that the carcasses of all numbered from twenty years old and upward who murmured will fall in the wilderness, that their children will wander forty years, a year for each day of the forty-day search, and that only Caleb and Joshua will enter the land sworn to Israel.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the wilderness narrative: Numbers 32:13 records Israel wandering forty years until the generation that did evil was consumed, Deuteronomy 2:14 gives the same span, and Joshua 5:6 records that the nation wandered forty years until the men of war were consumed.
RelatedEvents: Wilderness Wanderings; The Twelve Spies and Israel's Unbelief

Prophecy: The Earth Shall Swallow Korah's Company
ProphecySummary: Moses sets a test: if Korah, Dathan and Abiram die a common death, the LORD has not sent him, but if the LORD makes a new thing and the earth opens her mouth and swallows them alive into the pit, then they have provoked the LORD.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled immediately in Numbers 16:31-33: as Moses finishes speaking, the ground cleaves asunder under them, the earth opens her mouth and swallows them, their houses, and all the men that appertained to Korah.
RelatedPeople: Moses; Aaron; Korah, Son of Izhar; Dathan; Abiram

Prophecy: Moses and Aaron Barred from the Land
ProphecySummary: Because Moses and Aaron did not sanctify God in the eyes of Israel at the waters of Meribah, God tells them they will not bring the congregation into the land he has given them.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in Deuteronomy 34:1-5: Moses views the land from Mount Nebo and dies there in the land of Moab, and does not cross over; Deuteronomy 32:48-52 restates the same sentence and is included as a retelling passage, not a separate entry.

Prophecy: Balaam: Israel's King Higher Than Agag
ProphecySummary: In his third oracle Balaam says Israel's seed will be in many waters, his king will be higher than Agag, his kingdom will be exalted, God brought him out of Egypt, he will eat up the nations his enemies, and he lies down as a lion that none will stir up, with blessing on those who bless him and cursing on those who curse him.
Fulfillment: Debated, stated as such: the oracle's king is not named, so whether 'higher than Agag' points to Saul's defeat of Agag, King of Amalek (1 Samuel 15), to David's wider victories, or to a later king is not settled by the passage itself. The blessing-and-cursing line repeats the Abrahamic promise already covered by a live row and is not counted here as a new prediction; this entry covers only the king-above-Agag exaltation, which the live Balaam rows do not include, since they cite Numbers 23:7-10, 23:18-24 and 24:20-24 but not 24:7-9.
RelatedPeople: Balaam; Balak; Agag, King of Amalek

Prophecy: Phinehas: A Covenant of Everlasting Priesthood
ProphecySummary: After Phinehas turns away God's wrath in the matter of Baal-peor, God gives him his covenant of peace, and says he and his seed after him will have the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for Israel.
Fulfillment: Partly fulfilled: the priesthood continues through Phinehas and his son Eleazar's line, notably in the Zadokite line, but the priesthood's later disruption and the question of how far 'everlasting' extends beyond that line mean the promise is not marked as simply closed.

Prophecy: Remaining Inhabitants Shall Be Pricks and Thorns
ProphecySummary: God warns that if Israel does not drive out the inhabitants of the land, those left remaining will be pricks in their eyes and thorns in their sides, will vex them in the land, and God will do to Israel as he thought to do to those inhabitants.
Fulfillment: Partly fulfilled: Judges 2:3 records the LORD saying the remaining nations will be as thorns in Israel's sides, and the book of Judges shows those nations vexing Israel repeatedly. It is a conditional warning, marked partial because the vexing recurs across generations rather than ending in one event.

Prophecy: Sihon and Og Delivered into Israel's Hand
ProphecySummary: At the Arnon, God tells Israel to begin to possess Sihon's land and contend with him in battle, and to put dread and fear of Israel on the nations; before Og of Bashan he says, fear him not, for I will deliver him, all his people and his land into Israel's hand, as was done to Sihon.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in Deuteronomy 2:32-3:11: Sihon comes out to battle and is smitten with his sons and all his people, and Og is likewise defeated, his cities taken and his land possessed.

Prophecy: Apostasy After Moses, and the Song as Witness
ProphecySummary: God tells Moses that after his death the people will rise up and go whoring after the gods of strangers in the land, forsake him and break his covenant; Moses says he knows that after his death they will utterly corrupt themselves, turn aside from the way commanded, and evil will befall them in the latter days. The Song of Moses is appointed as a witness against them, foretelling that Israel will forsake God, provoke him with vanities, and be moved to jealousy by those who are not a people.
Fulfillment: Partly fulfilled: the Judges cycle and the later history of the kings show Israel repeatedly forsaking God for other gods and suffering the evils foretold, while the 'latter days' horizon of Deuteronomy 31:29 keeps the pattern open rather than closed in a single event.

Prophecy: Moses' Blessings on the Tribes
ProphecySummary: Before his death Moses blesses each tribe in turn: Reuben to live and not die, Judah to be brought to his people, Levi to bear Urim and Thummim and teach Israel, Benjamin to dwell safely by the LORD, Joseph blessed with precious things of heaven and earth, Zebulun and Issachar rejoicing in going out and in tents, Gad enlarged dwelling as a lion, Dan a lion's whelp leaping from Bashan, Naphtali satisfied with favour, and Asher blessed with children and dipping his foot in oil. Simeon receives no separate blessing in this chapter, and none is invented for him.
Fulfillment: Partly fulfilled, tribe by tribe rather than as a single event: Levi's teaching and priestly role, Joseph's fruitfulness in Ephraim and Manasseh, and Gad's and Dan's martial descriptions find counterparts in the settlement and later history, while several blessings are open-ended characterisations rather than dated events, so the grouped entry is not marked simply fulfilled. Grouped as one entry, mirroring the live row that groups Jacob's blessings on his sons.
RelatedPeople: Moses; Reuben; Levi; Judah; Benjamin; Joseph, Son of Jacob; Zebulun; Issachar; Gad; Dan; Naphtali; Asher

Prophecy: The Conquest Promised to Joshua
ProphecySummary: At the Jordan, the LORD tells Joshua that Israel will cross over and take the land sworn to their fathers, that every place their feet tread is given to them, and that no man will be able to stand against Joshua all his life.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the conquest narrative: Israel crosses the Jordan, takes Jericho, Ai, and the southern and northern coalitions, and Joshua 21:43-45 records that the LORD gave Israel all the land sworn to their fathers and that none of his good promises failed.

Prophecy: The Fall of Jericho Foretold
ProphecySummary: Before the march begins, the LORD tells Joshua that Jericho, its king, and its mighty men are given into his hand, and that after seven days of circling the city the wall will fall flat when the trumpets sound and the people shout.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled exactly as spoken: after the seventh-day circuit, trumpet blast, and shout, the wall falls and Israel takes the city (Joshua 6:20). Distinct from the separate curse on whoever later rebuilds Jericho, which is already a live row.

Prophecy: Ai Given into Joshua's Hand
ProphecySummary: After the first defeat at Ai, the LORD tells Joshua not to fear, to take all the people of war, and that the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land are given into Joshua's hand, with an ambush to be laid behind the city.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled when the ambush takes the city and its defenders are defeated (Joshua 8:19-21). The prediction is distinct from the Jericho oracle: a new campaign, a new city, and a different tactic.

Prophecy: The Southern Kings Delivered at Gibeon
ProphecySummary: When five Amorite kings march against Gibeon, the LORD tells Joshua not to fear them, for they are delivered into his hand and not one of them will stand before him.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled the same day: the LORD discomfits the coalition before Israel at Gibeon (Joshua 10:10), and the campaign ends with the kings' defeat.

Prophecy: The Northern Kings Delivered at Merom
ProphecySummary: Before the battle at the waters of Merom, the LORD tells Joshua not to fear the great northern coalition, for by the next day at that time he will deliver them up all slain before Israel, whose horses are to be hamstrung and chariots burned.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled the next day: Joshua comes suddenly upon the coalition at Merom and the LORD delivers them into Israel's hand (Joshua 11:7-8).

Prophecy: Joshua's Farewell Warning of Dispossession
ProphecySummary: In his farewell addresses Joshua warns that if Israel goes back, intermarries with the remaining nations, and serves other gods, the LORD will no more drive those nations out, they will become snares and thorns, and Israel will perish from the good land.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in stages: the remaining nations become snares in the Judges period, when Israel dwells among them and serves their gods (Judges 3:5-6), and the warning reaches its end in the exile from the land (2 Kings 25:1-21).

Prophecy: Judah Shall Go Up First
ProphecySummary: After Joshua's death Israel asks who will go up first against the Canaanites, and the LORD answers that Judah shall go up, for the land is delivered into his hand.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled at once: Judah goes up, the LORD delivers the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hand, and they take Jerusalem (Judges 1:4, 1:8).

Prophecy: The Nations Left as Thorns at Bochim
ProphecySummary: At Bochim the angel of the LORD rebukes Israel for making leagues and sparing altars, and declares that because of their disobedience he will not drive the remaining nations out; they will be as thorns in Israel's sides and their gods a snare.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled throughout Judges: Israel dwells among the remaining peoples, intermarries, and serves their gods (Judges 3:5-6), and the nations repeatedly oppress them in the cycles that follow.

Prophecy: Jotham's Curse on Abimelech and Shechem
ProphecySummary: From Mount Gerizim Jotham tells the parable of the trees and the bramble, ending with a curse: if Shechem dealt falsely with Jerubbaal's house, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour Shechem and the house of Millo, and let fire come out from Shechem and Millo and devour Abimelech.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in mutual destruction: God renders Abimelech's wickedness in slaying his seventy brothers and the evil of the men of Shechem upon their own heads, and the narrative states that upon them came the curse of Jotham (Judges 9:56-57).
RelatedPeople: Jotham, Son of Gideon; Abimelech, Son of Gideon

Prophecy: Benjamin Delivered on the Third Day
ProphecySummary: After two defeats before Gibeah, Israel asks through Phinehas whether to go out again against Benjamin, and the LORD answers to go up, for tomorrow he will deliver Benjamin into their hand.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled the next day: the LORD smites Benjamin before Israel (Judges 20:35), ending the civil war at Gibeah.

Prophecy: Hannah's Song: The LORD Exalts His Anointed
ProphecySummary: In her song Hannah proclaims a pattern of divine reversal, the poor raised to sit among princes, and ends by looking forward: the adversaries of the LORD will be broken, the LORD will judge the ends of the earth, and he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.
Fulfillment: The reversal pattern is fulfilled repeatedly in the Samuel narrative, and the anointed-king language is fulfilled in David's rise to the throne (2 Samuel 5:3). Whether the final line points beyond David to a future Messiah is disputed, so the entry is marked Debated rather than claimed as settled.

Prophecy: Samuel's Warning: The Manner of the King
ProphecySummary: When Israel demands a king, Samuel warns what the king they choose will do: he will take their sons for chariots and armies, their daughters for his household, their fields, vineyards, and flocks, a tenth of their seed and sheep, and they will become his servants and cry out under him.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled under the monarchy: the people's own later complaint is that Solomon made their yoke grievous (1 Kings 12:4), and the pattern of royal seizure runs through the kings, climaxing in Ahab's seizure of Naboth's vineyard (1 Kings 21).

Prophecy: Samuel's Signs to Saul
ProphecySummary: At Saul's anointing Samuel predicts three signs for that same day: two men at Rachel's sepulchre reporting the lost asses found, three men on the road to Bethel sharing bread, and a company of prophets at the hill of God, where the Spirit will come on Saul, he will prophesy, and be turned into another man.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled the same day: all the signs come to Saul, God gives him another heart, and he prophesies among the prophets (1 Samuel 10:9-13).

Prophecy: Samuel's Warning: Consumed, You and Your King
ProphecySummary: In his farewell Samuel sets the condition plainly: if Israel will not obey the voice of the LORD but rebels, the hand of the LORD will be against them, and if they still do wickedly they will be consumed, both they and their king.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled first in Saul's own fall with his sons on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:6), and the same pattern runs to the monarchy's end in the exile of king and people (2 Kings 25).

Prophecy: Abigail's Sure House for David
ProphecySummary: Interceding for Nabal's household, Abigail tells David that the LORD will certainly make him a sure house because he fights the battles of the LORD, that his soul will be bound in the bundle of life while his enemies are slung away, and that the LORD will appoint him ruler over Israel.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled when David is anointed king over all Israel (2 Samuel 5:3) and, more fully, in Nathan's dynastic oracle promising David an everlasting house (2 Samuel 7:16), which is already a live row; Abigail's word is the earlier, separate occasion.

Prophecy: Samuel at Endor: Saul and His Sons Fall Tomorrow
ProphecySummary: Through the medium at Endor, Samuel tells Saul that the LORD will deliver Israel with him into the hand of the Philistines, and that tomorrow Saul and his sons will be with him, and the host of Israel delivered to the Philistines.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled the next day on Mount Gilboa: Saul's sons fall, Saul falls on his sword, and Israel flees before the Philistines (1 Samuel 31:1-6).
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Jonathan, Son of Saul

Prophecy: David Shall Surely Overtake and Recover All at Ziklag
ProphecySummary: Finding Ziklag burned and his people carried off, David enquires of the LORD whether to pursue the troop, and the LORD answers: pursue, for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the pursuit: David recovers all that the Amalekites had carried away, and nothing is lacking, small or great (1 Samuel 30:18-19).

Prophecy: David's Two Victories over the Philistines Foretold
ProphecySummary: Twice David enquires of the LORD against the Philistines in the valley of Rephaim. First the LORD says to go up, for he will doubtless deliver the Philistines into David's hand. The second time the LORD says not to go up directly but to circle behind them, and when the sound of marching is heard in the mulberry trees, then the LORD will go out before him to smite the Philistine host.
Fulfillment: Both victories follow as spoken: David smites the Philistines at Baal-perazim (2 Samuel 5:20) and again from Geba to Gazer after the mulberry-tree signal (2 Samuel 5:25). The pair is kept as one entry following the live set's precedent for paired victories.

Prophecy: The Sword Shall Never Depart from David's House
ProphecySummary: After David's sin with Bathsheba, Nathan declares that because David despised the LORD and took Uriah's wife, the sword will never depart from his house, and the LORD will raise up evil against him out of his own house, taking his wives before his eyes and giving them to his neighbour in the sight of the sun.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the strife that follows within David's house: Amnon is slain (2 Samuel 13:28-29), and Absalom rises against his father and takes his concubines publicly (2 Samuel 15:13-14; 16:21-22). This entry covers the house-strife prediction; the child's death is a separate prediction drafted separately.
RelatedPeople: Nathan; King David; Absalom; Amnon, Son of David

Prophecy: The Child of David and Bathsheba Shall Die
ProphecySummary: Nathan adds a distinct sentence to his judgment on David: because by this deed David gave great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child born to him shall surely die.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled within days: the child becomes sick and dies on the seventh day (2 Samuel 12:18-19), despite David's fasting and prayer.
RelatedPeople: Nathan; King David; Bathsheba; Uriah the Hittite

Prophecy: Solomon's Prayer: Exile and Return Foretold
ProphecySummary: At the temple dedication Solomon foresees the sequence: if Israel sins, the LORD will be angry and deliver them to the enemy, who will carry them captive far or near; yet if in captivity they bethink themselves, repent, and pray toward their land, the LORD will hear, maintain their cause, forgive them, and give them compassion before their captors.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the Babylonian captivity, when Judah is carried away (2 Kings 25:11), and in the return under Cyrus, who proclaims that the LORD has charged him to build the house at Jerusalem (Ezra 1:1-3). Drafted with hesitation noted in the report: the passage is cast as prayer and condition, not as a bare oracle.
RelatedEvents: Building of Solomon's Temple; Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Prophecy: Warning to Solomon's House: Israel Cut Off, the Temple Cast Out
ProphecySummary: After the dedication the LORD warns Solomon and his children: if they turn from following him, serve other gods, and worship them, he will cut off Israel from the land he gave them, cast the hallowed house out of his sight, and Israel will become a proverb and a byword, with passers-by hissing at the ruined house.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled when Nebuzaradan burns the house of the LORD and breaks down Jerusalem's walls (2 Kings 25:8-10), after the long apostasy of the kings.
RelatedEvents: Building of Solomon's Temple; Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Prophecy: The Man of God from Judah Shall Die
ProphecySummary: After the man of God from Judah disobeys the LORD's command and eats and drinks at Bethel, an old prophet cries against him by the word of the LORD: because he has not kept the commandment, his carcase shall not come to the sepulchre of his fathers.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled on the road home: a lion meets him and slays him, and his body is brought back and buried in the old prophet's own sepulchre, not his fathers' (1 Kings 13:24-26). Companion to the already-live Josiah prophecy from the same visit; this is the man's own separate sentence.

Prophecy: Jehu's Judgment on the House of Baasha
ProphecySummary: The word of the LORD comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha: because Baasha walked in Jeroboam's way and made Israel sin, the LORD will take away the posterity of Baasha and his house and make it like the house of Jeroboam, with the dogs eating those who die in the city and the birds those who die in the fields.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled when Zimri destroys all the house of Baasha and leaves him none that pisseth against the wall, according to the word of the LORD by Jehu the prophet (1 Kings 16:11-12).
RelatedPeople: Jehu, Son of Hanani; Baasha, King of Israel; Jeroboam

Prophecy: The Widow's Meal and Oil Shall Not Fail
ProphecySummary: At Zarephath Elijah tells the widow that, by the word of the LORD God of Israel, the barrel of meal shall not waste and the cruse of oil shall not fail until the day the LORD sends rain on the earth.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled through the drought: she and her household eat many days, and the barrel of meal wastes not and the cruse of oil fails not, according to the word of the LORD by Elijah (1 Kings 17:15-16). The drought itself is already a live row; this is the separate provision word.

Prophecy: The Prophet's Sentence on Ahab: Life for Life
ProphecySummary: After Ahab releases Ben-hadad alive, a prophet tells him by the word of the LORD: because thou hast let go a man appointed to utter destruction, thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled at Ramoth-gilead: a bowman draws at a venture and wounds Ahab, who dies that day, and his blood is washed in the pool of Samaria as the LORD had spoken (1 Kings 22:34-38). Distinct from Micaiah's separate Ramoth-gilead prophecy, which is already a live row.

Prophecy: Elijah: Ahaziah Shall Surely Die
ProphecySummary: When Ahaziah, sick from a fall, sends to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron, Elijah meets the messengers with the word of the LORD: because there is no God in Israel to enquire of, Ahaziah shall not come down from the bed he has gone up to, but shall surely die.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled as spoken: Ahaziah dies according to the word of the LORD which Elijah had spoken (2 Kings 1:17), and Jehoram reigns in his stead.

Prophecy: Elisha's Healed Waters at Jericho
ProphecySummary: At the spring of Jericho Elisha casts in salt and declares by the word of the LORD: I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled as stated in the narrative: the waters are healed unto this day, according to the saying that Elisha spake (2 Kings 2:22), with no later reversal recorded in Scripture.

Prophecy: Gehazi's Leprosy for Ever
ProphecySummary: After Gehazi takes Naaman's gifts by deceit, Elisha pronounces that the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to Gehazi and to his seed for ever.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled at once: Gehazi goes out from Elisha's presence a leper as white as snow (2 Kings 5:27). The hereditary extent is stated in the sentence itself and is not separately traced in the narrative.

Prophecy: The Seven-Year Famine Foretold to the Shunammite
ProphecySummary: Elisha warns the woman whose son he had restored to life to leave with her household and sojourn wherever she can, for the LORD has called for a famine, and it will come upon the land seven years.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled over the seven years: she sojourns in the land of the Philistines seven years, returns at the end of the seven years, and appeals to the king for her house and land (2 Kings 8:2-3, 8:6). Distinct from the already-live promise of her son's birth.

Prophecy: Solomon, a Man of Rest, Shall Build the House
ProphecySummary: A son will be born to David, named Solomon, who will be a man of rest with peace from his enemies, and he will build a house for the name of the LORD, with his kingdom established.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in part and pointing beyond Solomon: Solomon built the temple in Jerusalem and enjoyed rest and peace in his reign, as recorded in Kings. The promise of a throne established for ever was not exhausted by Solomon, whose kingdom later divided, so the everlasting aspect awaits its full fulfilment in David's greater Son.
RelatedEvents: Building of Solomon's Temple; Davidic Covenant

Prophecy: Hanani: Asa Shall Have Wars from Henceforth
ProphecySummary: Because Asa relied on the king of Syria instead of the LORD, the Syrian host escaped his hand, and from that time on Asa would have wars.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the narrative that follows: the long peace of Asa's earlier reign ends, with Baasha of Israel building Ramah against Judah in the thirty-sixth year of Asa, and warfare marking his later years.
RelatedPeople: Hanani, the Seer; King Asa; Baasha, King of Israel; Ben-hadad, King of Syria

Prophecy: Elijah's Letter: Jehoram Struck with Plague and Bowel Disease
ProphecySummary: Because Jehoram of Judah walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, made Judah go astray, and slew his better brothers, a great plague would strike his people, children, wives, and goods, and he himself would suffer a wasting bowel disease until his bowels fell out.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled as narrated in the same chapter: Philistines and Arabians carried away Jehoram's substance, sons, and wives, leaving only his youngest son, and afterwards the LORD struck him with an incurable bowel disease from which he died after two years.

Prophecy: God Has Determined to Destroy Amaziah
ProphecySummary: After Amaziah brought home the gods of Edom and worshipped them, and refused the prophet's counsel, the prophet declared that God had determined to destroy him.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in Amaziah's downfall: defeated and captured by Joash of Israel at Beth-shemesh, Jerusalem's wall broken down and its treasures taken, and after he turned away from following the LORD a conspiracy was made against him in Jerusalem and he was slain at Lachish.
RelatedPeople: Amaziah, King of Judah; Joash, King of Israel

Prophecy: Zeresh: Haman Shall Surely Fall Before Mordecai
ProphecySummary: After Haman told his wife Zeresh and his friends how Mordecai had been honoured, they told him that if Mordecai was of Jewish descent, before whom he had begun to fall, he would not prevail against him but would surely fall before him.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled within the same narrative: that very evening Haman was brought to Esther's banquet, his plot against Mordecai and the Jews was exposed, and he was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.

Prophecy: Job Shall Pray for His Friends and Be Accepted
ProphecySummary: The LORD told Eliphaz that Job would pray for him and his two friends, and that Job would be accepted, so that God would not deal with them according to their folly.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled immediately in the narrative: Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar did as commanded, offered the burnt offering, Job prayed for them, and the LORD accepted Job.

Prophecy: Not One of His Bones Broken
ProphecySummary: The righteous sufferer is kept by the LORD so that not one of his bones is broken.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled at the crucifixion: John's Gospel records that the soldiers did not break Jesus' legs, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, a bone of him shall not be broken.

Prophecy: All Nations Shall Come and Worship, Counted as Born in Zion
ProphecySummary: All the nations God has made will come and worship before him and glorify his name; princes will come from Egypt and Ethiopia will stretch out her hands to God, and people from Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia will be counted as born in Zion when the LORD registers the peoples.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in the gathering of Gentiles into the worship of God, seen from the earliest Gentile conversions onward, but not yet fulfilled in the full sense of all nations coming to worship, so the complete gathering remains awaited.

Prophecy: The LORD Comes to Judge the Earth
ProphecySummary: The LORD is coming to judge the earth, and he will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity and truth.
Fulfillment: Awaited in its full and final sense: particular judgments in history do not exhaust a universal judgment of the whole earth, which Scripture elsewhere places at the end, so this remains a future fulfilment.

Prophecy: The LORD Shall Build Up Zion
ProphecySummary: The LORD will arise and have mercy on Zion when the set time to favour her has come; he will build up Zion and appear in his glory, the nations and kings will fear his name, a future people will be created to praise him, and peoples and kingdoms will be gathered to serve the LORD.
Fulfillment: Begun in the return from exile and the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the temple under Cyrus, Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah, when Zion was again inhabited and its name declared there; the full gathering of peoples and kingdoms to serve the LORD, and a people created to praise him, extend beyond that restoration and remain partially fulfilled.
RelatedPeople: Cyrus the Great; Zerubbabel; Ezra; Nehemiah
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Rebuilding of the Temple

Prophecy: Jerusalem's Stay and Staff Removed
ProphecySummary: The LORD will take away from Jerusalem and Judah every support of bread and water, along with its judges, warriors, prophets, elders and skilled leaders, leaving the city disordered and its finery stripped.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in substance in the Babylonian siege and exile, when Jerusalem lost its leadership and supplies; the chapter's stripping of finery matches a city under judgment rather than a single dated incident.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Prophecy: The Vineyard Laid Waste
ProphecySummary: God's vineyard, planted and tended with care but yielding wild grapes, will have its hedge removed and its wall broken down, be left unpruned and unwatered, and grow briers and thorns.
Fulfillment: The desolation of Judah and Jerusalem in the Babylonian conquest matches the vineyard laid waste; restoration afterwards does not undo the judgment the song announces.

Prophecy: Desolation Until Only a Tenth Remains
ProphecySummary: Asked how long his hardening message must run, Isaiah is told: until cities lie wasted without inhabitants, houses stand empty, the land is utterly desolate and the people are removed far away, yet a holy seed remains like a stump.
Fulfillment: The exile emptied Judah's cities and land, and a remnant returned; the holy-seed remnant is only partly realised in the return, so the entry is not claimed as wholly complete.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Prophecy: Ephraim Broken Within Sixty-Five Years
ProphecySummary: Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be broken so that it is no longer a people, its head Samaria and Samaria's head the son of Remaliah notwithstanding.
Fulfillment: Assyria conquered Samaria in 722 BC and deported its people, and later Assyrian resettlement broke Ephraim as a distinct people; the exact end-point of the sixty-five-year count is debated, so this is marked partial rather than exact.

Prophecy: Damascus and Samaria Plundered Before the Child Speaks
ProphecySummary: Before Isaiah's son Maher-shalal-hash-baz learns to say father or mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be carried away before the king of Assyria.
Fulfillment: Assyria plundered Damascus in 732 BC and Samaria in 722 BC, within the child's infancy and early childhood as the sign requires.

Prophecy: Egypt and Ethiopia Led Away Captive by Assyria
ProphecySummary: As Isaiah walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign, so the king of Assyria will lead away Egyptian prisoners and Ethiopian captives, young and old, naked and barefoot, to Egypt's shame.
Fulfillment: Assyria's campaigns against Egypt and Ethiopia in the late eighth century, including the Ashdod affair of Isaiah's day, produced captives in the manner described; this is distinct from the broader humbling of Egypt in Isaiah 19, which is already live.

Prophecy: The Crown of Pride of Ephraim Trodden Down
ProphecySummary: Woe to the fading crown of Ephraim's drunkards at Samaria: their glorious beauty will be cast down and trodden underfoot, like an early fig eaten as soon as it is seen.
Fulfillment: Samaria fell to Assyria in 722 BC and the northern kingdom's pride and capital were destroyed.

Prophecy: Ariel Besieged and Suddenly Delivered
ProphecySummary: Ariel, the city where David dwelt, will be distressed and besieged by encamped enemies, brought low to whisper from the dust, and then its multitude of foes will vanish suddenly, as a dream in the night.
Fulfillment: The Assyrian siege of Jerusalem in 701 BC, lifted suddenly with Sennacherib's army destroyed, fits the sudden deliverance; because Jerusalem was besieged again later, the entry is marked partial rather than tied to one siege alone.
RelatedPeople: Isaiah; King David; Sennacherib, King of Assyria

Prophecy: Egypt's Help Vain
ProphecySummary: Judah's envoys who go down to Egypt for help will find it vain and to no purpose: Egypt's strength is to sit still, and trusting in Pharaoh's horses and chariots will bring shame, not deliverance.
Fulfillment: Egypt failed to save Judah from Assyria in 701 BC and failed again against Babylon; Judah's Egyptian alliance repeatedly proved empty.

Prophecy: A King Reigns in Righteousness and the Spirit Is Poured Out
ProphecySummary: A king will reign in righteousness with princes ruling in judgment, and afterwards the Spirit will be poured out from on high, turning wilderness into fruitful field and bringing justice, quietness and assurance.
Fulfillment: No merely historical Judahite king matches the whole picture; the righteous reign and the outpouring of the Spirit are inaugurated in the New Testament but await their full realisation, so this is partial, not yet complete.

Prophecy: The Servants Blessed, the Rebels Judged
ProphecySummary: In contrast to rebels who forsake the LORD and prepare a table for fortune, God's servants will eat, drink and rejoice while the rebels go hungry, thirsty and ashamed, and be slain, leaving their name as a curse.
Fulfillment: The distinction between a preserved servant remnant and a judged rebellious generation runs through the exile and beyond, but its final separation is not yet complete, hence partial.

Prophecy: Judgment by Fire and the Nations Gathered to Jerusalem
ProphecySummary: The LORD will come with fire and whirlwind chariots to judge all flesh, gather all nations and tongues to see his glory, send survivors to the distant coastlands to declare it, and bring worshippers from all nations to his holy mountain.
Fulfillment: No historical event gathers all nations to Jerusalem in this way or completes the fire judgment; this remains awaited, distinct from the new-heavens entry already live, which rests on Isaiah 65:17-25.

Prophecy: Evil Neighbours Plucked Up and Restored
ProphecySummary: God's evil neighbours who touch Israel's inheritance will be plucked out of their land, and Judah too will be plucked up; afterwards, if the plucked nations learn the ways of God's people, they will be built in the midst of his people, but a nation that will not obey will be utterly plucked up and destroyed.
Fulfillment: Babylon's campaigns plucked Judah's neighbours as well as Judah; the conditional restoration depended on obedience and was never realised as a wholesale building of those nations among God's people, so this is partial.

Prophecy: Tophet Renamed the Valley of Slaughter
ProphecySummary: The place called Tophet and the Valley of the son of Hinnom will no longer bear those names but will be called the Valley of Slaughter, because its people filled it with innocent blood, burned their children, and will themselves fall by the sword and lie unburied.
Fulfillment: Jerusalem's slaughter in 586 BC, with bodies left unburied around the city, matches the renaming; the valley's defilement under Josiah is a separate earlier act, not this prediction's fulfilment.

Prophecy: Pashhur Made a Terror and Carried to Babylon
ProphecySummary: Pashhur, who struck Jeremiah and put him in the stocks, will become a terror to himself and his friends, see them fall by the sword, and himself go to Babylon and die there, with all Judah's wealth given to Babylon.
Fulfillment: Judah's wealth and people were indeed carried to Babylon, and Pashhur's party shared that captivity; no surviving narrative separately records Pashhur's death in Babylon, so the personal detail is not claimed as independently confirmed.

Prophecy: Shallum Shall Not Return
ProphecySummary: Shallum son of Josiah, who reigned in his father's place and went out from Jerusalem, will not return to this place but will die where he was carried captive.
Fulfillment: Jehoahaz, also called Shallum, was taken to Egypt by Pharaoh Necho and died there, as 2 Kings 23:34 records; this is distinct from the Coniah entry already live, which concerns a different king.
RelatedPeople: Jeremiah; Shallum, Son of Josiah; King Josiah

Prophecy: The Scattered Remnant Gathered Under Shepherds
ProphecySummary: Woe to shepherds who scatter God's flock: he will gather the remnant out of all countries where he drove them, bring them back to their folds, and set shepherds over them who will feed them so they fear no more.
Fulfillment: The return from Babylon gathered only part of the scattered remnant, and the fear-free shepherding is not yet complete; this entry uses Jeremiah 23:1-4 and 23:7-8 only, leaving the Righteous Branch verses already live untouched.

Prophecy: Good Figs Preserved, Bad Figs Scattered
ProphecySummary: Like good figs, the exiles carried to Babylon will be acknowledged for good, given a heart to know the LORD, and brought back; like bad figs that cannot be eaten, Zedekiah, his princes and the remnant in Jerusalem and Egypt will be made a reproach, scattered, and consumed by sword, famine and pestilence.
Fulfillment: The Babylonian exiles were preserved and a remnant returned, while Zedekiah was captured and blinded and the Egypt remnant perished, matching the two fates.

Prophecy: The Cup of Wrath for All Nations
ProphecySummary: Jeremiah is made to take the wine cup of God's fury and give every nation to which he is sent to drink it, beginning with Jerusalem and Judah and running through Egypt, Philistia, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, Arabia and Babylon itself, until all drink, stagger and fall.
Fulfillment: Babylon's campaigns in turn brought these nations under judgment, and Babylon itself drank last; the sequence was fulfilled in history, though the cup's fullest, final sense remains open, hence partial.
Places: Jerusalem; Egypt; Tyre; Edom; Moab; Ammon; Babylon; Arabia

Prophecy: The Yoke of Nebuchadnezzar
ProphecySummary: God has given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his servant, and the nations that put their necks under Babylon's yoke will live, while the nation that will not serve him will be punished with sword, famine and pestilence until consumed.
Fulfillment: Judah and the surrounding nations did serve Babylon for a generation, and those that rebelled, including Judah under Zedekiah, were punished as described.

Prophecy: Jerusalem Rebuilt and Never Thrown Down
ProphecySummary: The city will be rebuilt to the LORD from the Tower of Hananeel to the Corner Gate, the measuring line will go out to Gareb and Goath, the whole valley of dead bodies and ashes will be holy, and the city will never again be plucked up or thrown down.
Fulfillment: Jerusalem was rebuilt after the exile along lines recalling this measure, but it was thrown down again in AD 70, so the never-thrown-down clause is not literally complete; this entry is partial and distinct from the general return entry already live.

Prophecy: David's Line and the Levitical Priests Endure
ProphecySummary: David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of Israel, the Levitical priests will never lack a man to offer sacrifice before God, and these covenants stand as firmly as day and night; if they could be broken, so could God's covenant with Israel.
Fulfillment: After the exile there was no reigning Davidic king and, after AD 70, no Levitical temple sacrifice, so how this promise endures is genuinely disputed between messianic, spiritualised and future readings; the doubt is stated, not resolved, and this is marked Debated.

Prophecy: The Remnant Fleeing to Egypt Will Perish There
ProphecySummary: The remnant of Judah that sets its face to enter Egypt, against God's warning, will die there by sword, famine and pestilence, with only a small number escaping, and Egypt, sought as refuge, will become their grave.
Fulfillment: The remnant that fled to Egypt after Gedaliah's murder was caught in Egypt's own disasters and largely perished there, with only a few escaping, as Jeremiah warned.

Prophecy: Pharaoh-Hophra Delivered to His Enemies
ProphecySummary: As Zedekiah was given into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, so Pharaoh-Hophra king of Egypt will be given into the hand of his enemies and of those who seek his life.
Fulfillment: Hophra (the Apries of Egyptian history) was deposed by his rival Amasis and lost his throne and life, matching delivery to his enemies; this is distinct from the general Egypt judgment already live, which rests on Jeremiah 46.

Prophecy: An Everlasting Covenant Remembered
ProphecySummary: After Jerusalem's shame is laid bare, God will nevertheless remember his covenant with her in the days of her youth and establish with her an everlasting covenant, so that she remembers, is confounded, and never opens her mouth again because of her shame.
Fulfillment: The return from exile began this remembering, but the everlasting covenant and the silencing of shame are only partly realised in history, so this is partial.

Prophecy: A Tender Twig Planted on a High Mountain
ProphecySummary: God will take a tender twig from the top of the high cedar, plant it on a high mountain of Israel, and it will become a goodly cedar under which birds of every wing will dwell, while all trees know that God brings down the high tree and exalts the low.
Fulfillment: Whether the twig is Zerubbabel, the restored Davidic governor, or the Messiah, or both in a layered sense, is genuinely contested, so the referent doubt is stated and this is marked Debated rather than assigned to one reading.

Prophecy: Gathered with an Outstretched Arm, Rebels Purged
ProphecySummary: God will rule over his scattered people with a mighty hand and fury poured out, bring them into the wilderness of the peoples to plead with them face to face, purge out the rebels, and bring the remainder into the land of Israel with acceptance.
Fulfillment: The return from Babylon gathered only part of the scattered people and no wilderness purging of rebels on this scale is recorded, so the gathering is begun but not complete.

Prophecy: The Sword Against Ammon
ProphecySummary: The drawn, polished sword is against the Ammonites for their reproach: it will devour, and Ammon will be given to fire, its blood in the midst of the land, remembered no more.
Fulfillment: Ammon as a distinct nation faded after Babylonian and later campaigns, but the exact agent and date of this sword judgment are not pinned by a single surviving narrative, so this is partial, and it is distinct from the Ammon judgment already live, which rests on Ezekiel 25:1-7.

Prophecy: Egypt Given to Nebuchadnezzar as Wages
ProphecySummary: Because Nebuchadnezzar's army laboured against Tyre with no wages, God will give him the land of Egypt, its multitude and spoil, as wages for his service against Tyre.
Fulfillment: A Babylonian campaign into Egypt in 568/567 BC is attested, but its extent and whether it amounted to taking Egypt's spoil on the scale described are debated, so this is partial with that doubt stated, and it is distinct from the general desolation of Egypt already live, which rests on Ezekiel 29:1-16.

Prophecy: Ruined Cities Rebuilt and the Land Fruitful
ProphecySummary: The mountains of Israel will shoot forth branches and yield fruit for God's people at hand to come, and in the day of cleansing the ruined cities will be inhabited, the wastes built, and the desolate land tilled like the garden of Eden, so the nations will know it was the LORD who built the ruins.
Fulfillment: Post-exilic rebuilding repopulated ruined towns and tilled the land again, but not on the Eden scale described, so this is partial; it uses Ezekiel 36:8-15 and 36:33-38 only, leaving the new-heart verses already live untouched.

Prophecy: Four Beasts, the Little Horn, and Judgment
ProphecySummary: Four great beasts rise from the sea, diverse from one another, and among the fourth beast's ten horns a little horn rises, speaking great things and wearing out the saints, until the Ancient of Days sits in judgment, the beast is slain, and the kingdom is given to the saints of the Most High for ever.
Fulfillment: The identities of the four beasts and the little horn are genuinely contested between ancient-empire, Antiochene and still-future readings, and the saints' everlasting possession is not yet complete, so this is marked Debated; the Son of Man verses already live (Daniel 7:13-14) are deliberately excluded from this entry's passages.

Prophecy: Edom's Cup and the End of Zion's Captivity
ProphecySummary: Daughter of Edom, rejoicing in the land of Uz, will herself drink the cup, be drunken and exposed; meanwhile the punishment of daughter of Zion is accomplished and he will no more carry her away into captivity, but will visit Edom's iniquity and discover her sins.
Fulfillment: Zion's Babylonian captivity did end with the return under Cyrus, and Edom was later subdued and lost its distinct standing, but the full visiting of Edom is not tied to a single dated event, so this is partial.

Prophecy: Ephraim Exiled to Egypt and Assyria
ProphecySummary: Hosea predicts that Ephraim will no longer dwell in the LORD's land but will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria, its sacrifices will cease to please God, its glory will fly away, and its people will be cast away as wanderers among the nations.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the Assyrian conquest of the northern kingdom and the deportation of Israel (722 BC), after which the ten tribes lived scattered among the nations and temple sacrifice in the land ceased.

Prophecy: The Calf of Beth-aven Carried to Assyria
ProphecySummary: Hosea predicts that the inhabitants of Samaria will mourn over the calves of Beth-aven, the calf itself will be carried to Assyria as a present to King Jareb, Samaria's king will be cut off like foam on water, and the high places of Aven will be destroyed and overgrown.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the fall of Samaria and the Assyrian removal of Israel's idolatrous cult objects; the northern monarchy ended and its calf worship came to an end.

Prophecy: Ransom from the Grave and Death
ProphecySummary: Hosea declares that God will ransom his people from the power of the grave and redeem them from death, saying to death that he will be its plagues and to the grave that he will be its destruction.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in Christ's resurrection, which the New Testament connects with this passage (1 Corinthians 15:54-55); the final defeat of death for all God's people is still awaited.

Prophecy: Revival After Two Days, Raised on the Third Day
ProphecySummary: Hosea pictures a returning people saying that after God has torn and smitten them, he will heal and bind them up, revive them after two days, and raise them up on the third day so they may live in his sight and know him as surely as the morning and the rain.
Fulfillment: Debated: some read this as Israel's restoration after judgment, others as pointing to Christ's resurrection on the third day. The passage itself does not name a single dated event, so neither reading is presented here as settled.

Prophecy: The Day of the LORD as Darkness
ProphecySummary: Amos warns those who long for the day of the LORD that it will be darkness and not light, very dark with no brightness in it, inescapable as fleeing a lion only to meet a bear, or leaning on a wall at home only to be bitten by a serpent.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in the darkness of judgment that fell on Israel in the Assyrian conquest; the passage also speaks in the language of a final day of the LORD that is still awaited.

Prophecy: Judgment Pronounced on Amaziah the Priest
ProphecySummary: Amos tells Amaziah, the priest of Bethel who opposed him, that his wife will become a harlot in the city, his sons and daughters will fall by the sword, his land will be divided by line, he will die in a polluted land, and Israel will surely go into captivity out of its land.
Fulfillment: Debated in its details: Scripture records the pronouncement but does not narrate Amaziah's personal fate, so the specific personal outcomes are stated here as predicted but not as historically confirmed; the captivity of Israel itself is confirmed.

Prophecy: The Altars of Bethel and the Houses of Ivory Destroyed
ProphecySummary: Amos predicts that when God visits Israel's transgressions he will also visit the altars of Bethel, the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground, and the winter house, summer house, houses of ivory, and great houses will perish.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the end of the northern kingdom's Bethel cult and its luxurious houses: Bethel's altar was later desecrated under Josiah (2 Kings 23:15-16) and the wealth of Samaria's elite perished with the kingdom.

Prophecy: Samaria Made a Heap of the Field
ProphecySummary: Micah predicts that God will make Samaria a heap of the field and like plantings of a vineyard, pour its stones into the valley, uncover its foundations, beat its graven images to pieces, and burn its hires with fire.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the Assyrian siege and capture of Samaria (722 BC), after which the city lost its standing as Israel's capital and its idolatrous images were destroyed.

Prophecy: Zion to Babylon, and There Delivered
ProphecySummary: Micah tells the daughter of Zion that she will go forth out of the city, dwell in the field, and go even to Babylon, and that there she will be delivered and redeemed from the hand of her enemies.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in the Babylonian exile of Judah and the return under Cyrus's decree; the fuller deliverance and redemption it pictures is treated in the live collection as still unfolding.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Prophecy: Deliverance from the Assyrian Invader
ProphecySummary: Micah predicts that when the Assyrian comes into the land and treads in the palaces, the promised ruler will be their peace, seven shepherds and eight principal men will be raised against the invader, and they will waste the land of Assyria with the sword and deliver the people from the Assyrian within their borders.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in the deliverance of Jerusalem from Sennacherib's invasion (701 BC), when the Assyrian army was turned back; the passage's fuller wasting of Assyria was completed only later with Assyria's fall, and its peace-ruler language points beyond that event.

Prophecy: War and Idolatry Cut Off in That Day
ProphecySummary: Micah predicts that in that day God will cut off horses and destroy chariots, cut off the cities of the land and throw down its strongholds, cut off witchcrafts, soothsayers, graven images, standing images, and groves, and execute vengeance on the heathen.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in the end of Judah's reliance on fortified cities and idolatry after the exile; the complete removal of war and idolatry it pictures is still awaited.

Prophecy: Judah's Yoke Broken, the Wicked Cut Off
ProphecySummary: Nahum tells afflicted Judah that God will afflict her no more, will break the Assyrian yoke from off her and burst her bonds in sunder, and that the bearer of good tidings of peace will come, so Judah may keep her feasts and vows, for the wicked will no more pass through her, being utterly cut off.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the fall of Nineveh (612 BC), which ended Assyria's domination of Judah; Judah's subsequent history shows the deliverance was from Assyria specifically, not from all later enemies.

Prophecy: Blessing from the Day of the Temple Foundation
ProphecySummary: Haggai tells the returned community to consider from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid, that although seed, vine, fig tree, pomegranate, and olive had not yet brought forth, from that day God will bless them.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in the completion of the Second Temple and the restored worship of the returned community; the passage gives no dated account of the agricultural blessing itself, so its full measure is not pinned to a single recorded event.

Prophecy: The Breaking of the Staves Beauty and Bands
ProphecySummary: Zechariah pictures the shepherd cutting asunder his staff Beauty to break the covenant made with all the people, and later cutting asunder his other staff Bands to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
Fulfillment: Debated: the passage is symbolic and its referent is disputed — readings include the breaking of God's covenant favour and of national unity at the rejection of the shepherd, and the passage itself names no dated historical event.

Prophecy: The Third Part Brought Through the Fire
ProphecySummary: Zechariah predicts that in all the land two parts will be cut off and die, but the third will be left, brought through the fire and refined as silver and tried as gold, calling on God's name and being heard, with God saying 'It is my people' and they saying 'The LORD is my God.'
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in the refining of a faithful remnant through successive judgments, including the destruction of Jerusalem; the final purified remnant it pictures is still awaited.

Prophecy: The Nations Keep the Feast of Tabernacles
ProphecySummary: Zechariah predicts that everyone left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year to year to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and keep the feast of tabernacles, and that any family of the earth, including Egypt, that does not go up will have no rain, but the plague with which God smites the nations that do not keep the feast.
Fulfillment: Future: no historical period shows all surviving nations annually worshipping in Jerusalem under this rain-and-plague sanction, so this is awaited as an end-time worship order.

Prophecy: The Refiner Purifies the Sons of Levi
ProphecySummary: Malachi asks who may abide the day of the messenger's coming, for he is like a refiner's fire and fullers' soap, and will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, purifying the sons of Levi and purging them as gold and silver so they may offer an offering in righteousness, and will come near to judgment as a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, and oppressors of the hireling, widow, fatherless, and stranger.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled in Christ's first coming, which exposed and judged corrupt worship and began the purification of God's people; the complete purification and judgment it pictures is still awaited.

Prophecy: The Book of Remembrance and the Jewels
ProphecySummary: Malachi predicts that those who fear the LORD and think upon his name will have a book of remembrance written before him, and in the day when he makes up his jewels they will be his and he will spare them as a man spares his own serving son, and then people will return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him who serves God and him who does not.
Fulfillment: Future: the day of the jewels and the open discernment between righteous and wicked has no completed historical fulfilment and is awaited at the final judgment.

Prophecy: The Day Burns as an Oven, the Sun of Righteousness Rises
ProphecySummary: Malachi predicts a coming day that will burn as an oven, when all the proud and all who do wickedly will be stubble burned up leaving neither root nor branch, but to those who fear God's name the Sun of righteousness will arise with healing in his wings, they will go forth and grow up as calves of the stall, and tread down the wicked as ashes under their feet in the day God does this.
Fulfillment: Future: this final day of burning judgment and healing for the God-fearing is not a completed historical event and is awaited.

Prophecy: Many from East and West Shall Sit Down in the Kingdom
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that many will come from the east and the west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, while the children of the kingdom who reject him will be cast out into outer darkness.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: Gentiles from every direction have entered the kingdom through faith in Christ, while unbelieving Israel was judged; the final banquet and final exclusion still lie ahead.

Prophecy: The Son of Man Shall Come Before the Cities of Israel Are Gone Over
ProphecySummary: Jesus tells his disciples, as he sends them out, that they will not have gone over the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
Fulfillment: Disputed: readings differ over whether this refers to the resurrection, the transfiguration, the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70, or the future return of Christ, so no single fulfilment is asserted here.

Prophecy: Christ Will Confess or Deny Each Person Before the Father
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that whoever confesses him before men, he will confess before his Father in heaven, and whoever denies him before men, he will deny before his Father.
Fulfillment: Awaited: this points to the future judgment-day confession and denial before the Father, which has not yet taken place.

Prophecy: Nineveh and the Queen of the South Shall Rise in Judgment
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that the men of Nineveh and the queen of the south will rise up in the judgment with his generation and condemn it, because they responded to Jonah and to Solomon while a greater one stands before that generation.
Fulfillment: Awaited: this points to the future judgment, when these past responders will stand as witnesses against the generation that rejected Christ.

Prophecy: Christ Will Build His Church
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that upon the rock he will build his church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: the church was founded at Pentecost and has endured through persecution and opposition; its final, unassailable triumph still lies ahead.

Prophecy: Some Standing Here Shall Not Taste Death Till They See the Son of Man Coming
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that some standing there will not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom, or the kingdom of God come with power.
Fulfillment: Disputed: this is commonly read as the transfiguration (which follows immediately in all three Gospels), the resurrection, or the fall of Jerusalem, and the saying's exact referent is not settled here.
RelatedPeople: Simon Peter; James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle

Prophecy: Those Who Forsake All Shall Receive a Hundredfold and Eternal Life
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that everyone who has forsaken houses, family, or lands for his name's sake shall receive a hundredfold (manifold more in this present time, with persecutions) and shall inherit everlasting life.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: believers have received manifold provision and fellowship in this life, with persecutions as Mark states, while the full inheritance of eternal life in the world to come is still awaited.

Prophecy: James and John Shall Drink of Christ's Cup
