ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that James and John shall indeed drink of his cup and be baptized with his baptism, sharing in his suffering, though places at his right and left are not his to give.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in their suffering for Christ: James was killed by Herod (Acts 12:2), and John suffered persecution and exile (Revelation 1:9).
RelatedPeople: James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle

Prophecy: The Kingdom Shall Be Taken and Given to a Fruit-Bearing Nation
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that the kingdom of God shall be taken from the chief priests and Pharisees who rejected him and given to a nation bringing forth its fruits.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: the kingdom's stewardship passed to a new people, Jew and Gentile believers bearing fruit, while the full fruitfulness of that people is still unfolding.

Prophecy: Your House Is Left Desolate Until You Say, Blessed Is He That Cometh
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that Jerusalem's house is left desolate and that its people will not see him again until they say, 'Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.'
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: Jerusalem was left desolate and the temple destroyed within a generation; the future acknowledgment of Christ by Jerusalem, implied by 'until', is still awaited.

Prophecy: The Woman's Anointing Shall Be Told Wherever the Gospel Is Preached
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that wherever the gospel is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done in anointing him will also be told for a memorial of her.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: the anointing is recorded in the Gospels and is retold wherever the gospel is preached, exactly as predicted.

Prophecy: Christ Shall Drink the Fruit of the Vine Anew in the Father's Kingdom
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that he will not drink again of the fruit of the vine until the day when he drinks it new with his disciples in his Father's kingdom.
Fulfillment: Awaited: this points to the future kingdom banquet, when Christ will drink anew with his people.

Prophecy: After Rising, Christ Will Meet His Disciples in Galilee
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that after he is risen again, he will go before his disciples into Galilee, where they will meet him.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: after the resurrection the disciples went into Galilee and saw the risen Jesus there (Matthew 28:16-17).

Prophecy: The Great Commission to All Nations
ProphecySummary: The risen Jesus commissions his disciples to teach all nations, baptizing them and teaching them to observe all he commanded, with his promise that he is with them always, even unto the end of the world.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: the gospel has been preached among all nations and Christ's promised presence has accompanied the church, while the task is not yet complete and the end of the world has not yet come. Note: Mark 16:15 stands in the disputed longer ending of Mark (see the signs draft).

Prophecy: Signs Shall Follow Them That Believe
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that signs shall follow them that believe: in his name they shall cast out devils, speak with new tongues, take up serpents unharmed, survive deadly drink, and lay hands on the sick so that they recover.
Fulfillment: Debated on two counts: these verses stand in the longer ending of Mark, whose text is disputed, and interpreters disagree over whether the signs describe the apostolic age, the whole church age, or a limited pattern. Acts records tongues, healings, and deliverances, but the serpent and poison clauses are not treated here as a settled promise for all believers.

Prophecy: Gabriel Foretells the Birth and Mission of John
ProphecySummary: The angel Gabriel predicts to Zechariah that his wife Elizabeth shall bear a son named John, who will be great, filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb, turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord, and go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: John was born to Zechariah and Elizabeth (Luke 1:57-66) and carried out the foretold ministry of turning many to the Lord and preparing the way.
RelatedPeople: Zechariah, Father of John the Baptist; Elizabeth; John the Baptist; Elijah

Prophecy: Simeon Foretells the Fall and Rising of Many and a Sword for Mary
ProphecySummary: Simeon predicts that the child Jesus is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel and for a sign spoken against, and that a sword shall pierce through Mary's own soul, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: responses to Jesus divided Israel, he was spoken against throughout his ministry, and Mary stood at the cross where the sword of grief pierced her (John 19:25).
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; The Crucifixion

Prophecy: Christ's Coming Shall Bring Fire and Division in Households
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that he has come to send fire on the earth and division rather than only peace: from henceforth households will be divided, father against son, mother against daughter, and in-law against in-law, over him.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: division over Jesus appears within households and communities throughout the Gospels and Acts, and has continued wherever the gospel divides responses to him.

Prophecy: Peter, Sifted by Satan, Shall Return and Strengthen His Brethren
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that Satan has desired to sift Peter as wheat, but that he has prayed for Peter's faith not to fail, and that when Peter is converted (turned back) he shall strengthen his brethren.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: Peter denied Christ, was restored after the resurrection (John 21:15-17), and strengthened his brethren as a leading witness in Acts.

Prophecy: The Repentant Thief Shall Be with Christ in Paradise Today
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts to the repentant criminal crucified beside him that on that very day he shall be with him in paradise.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: both died that day, and the promise was given as an accomplished assurance, not a distant hope.

Prophecy: Nathanael Shall See Heaven Opened and Angels Ascending and Descending
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts to Nathanael that hereafter he shall see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
Fulfillment: Disputed: the referent is unclear — readings include Jacob's ladder imagery fulfilled in Christ's ministry, the signs and resurrection appearances, and a future unveiling — so no single fulfilment is asserted here.

Prophecy: Worship Shall No Longer Be Tied to Gerizim or Jerusalem
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts to the Samaritan woman that the hour is coming when people will worship the Father neither on Mount Gerizim nor at Jerusalem, but true worshippers will worship in spirit and in truth.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: with the coming of Christ and the destruction of the Jerusalem temple, worship is no longer centred on either mountain, and spirit-and-truth worship has spread among all peoples.

Prophecy: Other Sheep Shall Be Brought into One Flock under One Shepherd
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that he has other sheep not of this fold, that he must bring them also, that they shall hear his voice, and that there shall be one flock and one shepherd.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: Gentile believers have been brought into the one flock under Christ, while the gathering of all his sheep is still ongoing.

Prophecy: Lazarus Shall Rise Again
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that Lazarus's sickness is not unto death but for God's glory, and tells Martha directly that her brother shall rise again.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled: Lazarus was raised from the tomb four days after his death (John 11:43-44).

Prophecy: One Man Shall Die for the Nation and Gather God's Scattered Children
ProphecySummary: Caiaphas, speaking as high priest, prophesies that it is expedient for one man to die for the people so the whole nation does not perish, and John explains that Jesus would die for that nation and also gather together in one the children of God scattered abroad.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: Jesus died for the nation, and the gathering of God's scattered children into one people began with Jew and Gentile believers and is still ongoing.

Prophecy: The Prince of This World Shall Be Cast Out
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that now is the judgment of this world and now shall the prince of this world be cast out, and that the prince of this world is judged.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: Satan's defeat was secured at the cross and resurrection, yet his final casting out (Revelation 20) still lies ahead, so the casting out is begun but not yet complete.

Prophecy: Believers Shall Do Greater Works Than These
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that he who believes in him shall do the works he does, and greater works than these, because he goes to his Father.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: the apostles' Spirit-empowered mission reached wider scope than Jesus's earthly ministry (Acts), and the mission continues; 'greater' is read here as greater in scope through his going to the Father, not greater in kind.

Prophecy: Disciples Shall Be Expelled from Synagogues and Killed as Service to God
ProphecySummary: Jesus predicts that the world will hate and persecute his disciples as it persecuted him, that they shall be put out of the synagogues, and that the time will come when whoever kills them will think he does God service, because their persecutors have not known the Father or him.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: synagogue expulsions and killings of believers are recorded in Acts and the early church, and the pattern of persecution for Christ's name has continued since.

Prophecy: Jesus Returns as He Ascended
ProphecySummary: As Jesus is taken up into heaven before the disciples' eyes, two men in white apparel announce that this same Jesus will come back in the same manner as they have seen him go into heaven.
Fulfillment: Awaited. The return itself has not yet occurred; the prediction fixes its manner (visibly, bodily, from heaven) rather than its date, and no date is stated.

Prophecy: The Times of Restitution of All Things
ProphecySummary: Peter announces that heaven must receive Jesus until the times of restitution of all things, when God will send Jesus Christ, who was preached beforehand, bringing times of refreshing from the presence of the Lord.
Fulfillment: Awaited. The sending of Christ and the restitution remain future; the passage itself places them after the present period in which heaven receives him, so they are not dated to the apostolic age.

Prophecy: Paul, Chosen Vessel Who Must Suffer
ProphecySummary: The Lord tells Ananias that Paul is a chosen vessel to bear Christ's name before Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel, and that he will be shown how great things he must suffer for Christ's name.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in the Acts narrative: Paul preaches to Gentiles, Jews, and rulers (including before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa), and suffers imprisonment, beatings, and opposition throughout his ministry. The same commission is restated when Paul recounts his calling in Acts 22 and Acts 26.

Prophecy: Paul to Bear Witness at Rome
ProphecySummary: After Paul's testimony in Jerusalem, the Lord stands by him at night and says that as he has testified in Jerusalem, so he must bear witness also at Rome.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled in Acts: Paul is sent to Rome under guard after his appeal to Caesar and preaches the kingdom of God there (Acts 28:16-31). Paul's earlier purpose to see Rome (Acts 19:21) is the same expectation, stated before the Lord's promise.

Prophecy: Paul Sees the Ephesian Elders No More
ProphecySummary: Farewelling the Ephesian elders at Miletus, Paul says he knows that all among whom he has preached the kingdom of God will see his face no more.
Fulfillment: Fulfilled within the Acts narrative: Paul goes on to Jerusalem, arrest, and Rome, and the narrative records no return to Ephesus. Later tradition about a possible release and return is outside Acts and is not treated here as overturning the narrative fulfilment.

Prophecy: An Appointed Day of Judgment by the Risen Man
ProphecySummary: Preaching at Athens, Paul says God has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man he has ordained, giving assurance of this by raising him from the dead.
Fulfillment: Awaited. The resurrection, cited as the assurance, has occurred; the appointed day of universal judgment itself has not yet occurred.

Prophecy: Creation Delivered and Bodies Redeemed
ProphecySummary: Paul says the glory to be revealed in believers outweighs present suffering, that creation itself will be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of God's children, and that believers groan awaiting the adoption, the redemption of the body.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled on the passage's own terms: believers already have the firstfruits of the Spirit, but creation's deliverance and the redemption of the body are still awaited.

Prophecy: The Judgment Seat of Christ
ProphecySummary: Paul says all will stand before the judgment seat of Christ, and everyone will give account of himself to God; in 2 Corinthians he restates it as all appearing before that seat to receive according to what was done in the body.
Fulfillment: Awaited. No such universal accounting before Christ has yet taken place; the 2 Corinthians passage is a restatement of the same prediction, not a separate one.

Prophecy: Satan Crushed Under Believers' Feet
ProphecySummary: Closing Romans, Paul says the God of peace will bruise Satan under the believers' feet shortly.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled on a begun-and-consummated reading: the early church's advance and deliverance from Satan's power began in the apostolic age, but Satan's final crushing is still awaited. The word 'shortly' is read here as nearness in God's purposes, not as a dated first-century consummation; this reading is noted so the merger can weigh it.

Prophecy: Works Tested by Fire on the Day
ProphecySummary: Paul says every man's work will be made manifest on the day, revealed by fire that tries its quality: work that abides receives a reward, work that burns brings loss, though the builder himself is saved yet so as by fire.
Fulfillment: Awaited. This testing day for believers' works has not yet occurred; it is distinct from the final judgment of the world in that the person tested is saved even when the work is lost.

Prophecy: Saints Judge the World and Angels
ProphecySummary: Paul says the saints will judge the world and will judge angels, arguing that believers therefore ought to be able to settle lesser disputes among themselves.
Fulfillment: Awaited. No such judging role for the saints has yet occurred; the passage states it as a future certainty, not as a present practice.

Prophecy: Resurrection Order and the End
ProphecySummary: Paul sets out the order of resurrection: Christ the firstfruits, afterward those who are Christ's at his coming, then the end, when Christ delivers up the kingdom to God the Father after putting down all rule, authority, and power, with death itself, the last enemy, destroyed, and the Son then subject to God that God may be all in all.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: Christ's resurrection as firstfruits has occurred, but the resurrection of those who are Christ's at his coming, the destruction of death, and the end itself are still awaited.

Prophecy: Trumpet Transformation and Death Swallowed Up
ProphecySummary: Paul reveals a mystery: not all will sleep, but all will be changed in a moment at the last trump, when the trumpet sounds, the dead are raised incorruptible, the living are changed, the corruptible puts on incorruption and the mortal puts on immortality, and death is swallowed up in victory.
Fulfillment: Awaited. The last trump, the raising of the dead incorruptible, and the change of the living have not yet occurred; this is the event-detail companion to the resurrection-order prediction, not a duplicate of it.

Prophecy: When the Perfect Comes, the Partial Is Done Away
ProphecySummary: Paul says present knowledge and prophecy are partial, but when that which is perfect comes, that which is in part will be done away, and believers will then know face to face, even as they are known.
Fulfillment: Disputed and unfulfilled on any reading: interpreters disagree whether 'that which is perfect' means the completion of revelation, the maturity of the church, or the consummation at Christ's coming, so no fulfilment date or event is asserted here. The doubt is stated rather than resolved.

Prophecy: All Things Gathered Together in Christ
ProphecySummary: Paul says God's purpose is that in the dispensation of the fullness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both things in heaven and things on earth.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: the gathering in Christ has begun through the church, but the full gathering of all things in heaven and on earth at the fullness of times is still awaited.

Prophecy: Every Knee Bows to Christ
ProphecySummary: Paul says that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, things in earth, and things under the earth, and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
Fulfillment: Partially fulfilled: confession of Jesus as Lord has begun among believers, but universal bowing and confession by all in heaven, earth, and under the earth is still awaited. Romans 14:11 cites the same Isaiah promise in the context of the judgment seat, and is included as a cross-reference; the judgment-seat entry itself is drafted separately.

Prophecy: The Saviour Transforms Bodies to His Glorious Body
ProphecySummary: Paul says believers' citizenship is in heaven, from where they look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will change their lowly bodies so they are fashioned like his glorious body, according to the power by which he can subdue all things to himself.
Fulfillment: Awaited. The Saviour's coming and the transformation of believers' bodies have not yet occurred; this states the same coming as the trumpet transformation from a different angle (likeness to Christ's glorious body), and the merger may fold it into that entry if it prefers one row per event.

Prophecy: The Lord Descends, the Dead Rise, the Living Are Caught Up
ProphecySummary: By the word of the Lord, Paul says those alive and remaining at the Lord's coming will not precede those who are asleep: the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout, the voice of the archangel, and the trump of God, the dead in Christ will rise first, and then the living remaining will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so be ever with the Lord.
Fulfillment: Awaited. The descent, the shout and trump, the rising of the dead in Christ first, and the catching up of the living have not yet occurred; the distinctive detail here (order of dead before living, meeting in the air) is what separates this entry from the generic second-coming rows.

Prophecy: The Day of the Lord Comes as a Thief, With Sudden Destruction
ProphecySummary: Paul says the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night: when people say 'Peace and safety', sudden destruction comes upon them like labour pains on a woman with child, and they will not escape.
Fulfillment: Awaited. The day of the Lord so described, with its sudden destruction on the unsuspecting, has not yet occurred; the 'Peace and safety' sign is the distinctive predictive detail of this entry.

Prophecy: The Lord Revealed in Flaming Fire
ProphecySummary: Paul says troubled believers will have rest when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, in flaming fire taking vengeance on those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel, who will be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, while he comes to be glorified in his saints and admired in all who believe.
Fulfillment: Awaited. The revelation from heaven with mighty angels, the vengeance in flaming fire, and the everlasting destruction described have not yet occurred.

Prophecy: The Final Shaking of Heaven and Earth
ProphecySummary: God promises one final shaking, not of the earth only but also of heaven, so that the things that are made and can be shaken are removed and only the things that cannot be shaken remain, leaving believers a kingdom that cannot be moved.
Fulfillment: Awaited as the final consummation: the created order has not yet been removed in this final sense, and the unshakeable kingdom is received by faith now and in full at the end. The shaking language echoes Haggai's promise of a shaking of heaven and earth.

Prophecy: The Crown of Life for Those Who Endure
ProphecySummary: The man who endures temptation and is tried will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love him.
Fulfillment: A promised future reward, not yet received in full: endurance is tested in this life, and the crown is given at the Lord's appearing. The same crown of life is promised to the faithful in Smyrna in Revelation.

Prophecy: Miseries Coming on the Oppressive Rich
ProphecySummary: Rich oppressors are told to weep and howl for the miseries that shall come upon them: their riches are corrupted, their rusted gold and silver will witness against them and eat their flesh like fire, and they have heaped up treasure for the last days while defrauding their labourers and living in wanton pleasure.
Fulfillment: Partially seen whenever ill-gotten wealth decays and oppressors face reckoning, and in the repeated falls of the powerful; the full reckoning at the judgment is still awaited, so the prediction is not yet exhausted.

Prophecy: Judgment Begins at the House of God
ProphecySummary: The time has come for judgment to begin at the house of God, and if it begins with believers first, the end of those who do not obey the gospel will be far worse; the righteous themselves are scarcely saved.
Fulfillment: Begun in the fiery trials and persecutions borne by the early church, which Peter presents as judgment beginning with God's own people; the final judgment of the disobedient is still awaited, so the prediction stands partly fulfilled.

Prophecy: The Crown of Glory at the Chief Shepherd's Appearing
ProphecySummary: When the chief Shepherd appears, faithful elders who shepherded God's flock willingly and by example will receive a crown of glory that does not fade.
Fulfillment: Awaited: the chief Shepherd has not yet appeared in this sense, and the unfading crown is a future reward for faithful shepherding, distinct from the crown of life promised to all who endure.

Prophecy: Fallen Angels Reserved for the Great Day
ProphecySummary: The angels who did not keep their first estate but left their own habitation are kept in everlasting chains under darkness, reserved for the judgment of the great day.
Fulfillment: Awaited: the angels are described as presently bound and reserved, and the great day of their judgment has not yet come. The same reservation of sinning angels for judgment is stated in 2 Peter.

Prophecy: Scoffers and Mockers in the Last Days
ProphecySummary: In the last days scoffers will come, walking after their own lusts and mocking the promise of the Lord's coming; the apostles had already warned that there would be mockers in the last time who walk after their own ungodly lusts.
Fulfillment: Seen through the church age in repeated mockery of the promise of Christ's coming and in teachers who follow their own lusts; the culmination at the end is still awaited, so the prediction is partly fulfilled.

Prophecy: Believers Made Like Christ at His Appearing
ProphecySummary: Believers are already sons of God, but what they shall be has not yet appeared; when Christ appears they shall be like him, for they shall see him as he is, and may then stand before him with confidence and not shame at his coming.
Fulfillment: Awaited: believers are not yet visibly like Christ, and the transformation is tied to his future appearing, when seeing him as he is makes them like him.

Prophecy: Warnings and Keeping Promised to the Seven Churches
ProphecySummary: Each of the seven churches in Asia receives a predictive word: Ephesus will lose its candlestick unless it repents; Smyrna will suffer tribulation ten days and must be faithful unto death; Pergamum will face Christ's sword unless it repents; Jezebel in Thyatira will be cast into a bed and her followers into great tribulation, and her children killed with death; Sardis will face Christ coming as a thief if it does not watch; the opponents of Philadelphia will come and worship before its feet; and Philadelphia will be kept from the hour of temptation that shall come upon all the world to try earth's dwellers.
Fulfillment: Debated: some read these as warnings fulfilled in the early history of those Asian churches, others as applying through the church age, and the worldwide hour of temptation in particular is variously placed in the past, the present age, or the end. The conditional form means repentance could avert the threatened judgment, so no single dated fulfilment can be asserted.
KeyPassages: Revelation 2:5; Revelation 2:10; Revelation 2:16; Revelation 2:22-23; Revelation 3:3; Revelation 3:9-10
Places: Ephesus; Smyrna; Pergamos; Thyatira; Sardis; Philadelphia; Laodicea

Prophecy: The Multitude from Great Tribulation Before the Throne
ProphecySummary: A great multitude that no one can number, from all nations and peoples and tongues, stands before the throne and before the Lamb in white robes; these are they who came out of great tribulation, washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb, and now serve God day and night in his temple, hungering and thirsting no more, with the Lamb feeding them and leading them to living fountains of waters while God wipes away every tear from their eyes.
Fulfillment: Debated: whether the great tribulation is a past persecution, the church's ongoing suffering, or a future end-time distress is disputed, and the same wiping away of tears is promised again at the new creation; the multitude's final state before the throne is therefore stated as the outcome without fixing its date.

Prophecy: The Holy City Trodden Forty-Two Months
ProphecySummary: John is told to measure the temple of God, the altar, and those who worship there, but to leave out the outer court, which is given to the Gentiles, and the holy city shall they tread under foot for forty-two months.
Fulfillment: Debated: the forty-two months match the beast's authority elsewhere in Revelation, but whether the trampling is the Roman destruction of Jerusalem, a future occupation, or a symbolic span of Gentile domination is disputed, and the measured temple is read as literal, symbolic, or heavenly by different interpreters.

Prophecy: The Everlasting Gospel Preached to Every Nation
ProphecySummary: An angel flies in mid-heaven with the everlasting gospel to preach to those who dwell on the earth, to every nation and kindred and tongue and people, announcing that the hour of God's judgment has come and calling all to fear God, give him glory, and worship the Maker of heaven and earth, sea, and fountains of waters.
Fulfillment: Debated: whether this is a literal angelic proclamation before the end, a symbolic picture of the church's worldwide preaching, or a final warning already in progress is disputed; a universal proclamation preceding judgment is the substance all readings share, and its completion is still awaited.

Prophecy: The Torment of the Beast-Worshippers
ProphecySummary: Anyone who worships the beast and his image and receives his mark in forehead or hand shall drink the wine of God's wrath poured out undiluted, and shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels and the Lamb, with the smoke of their torment rising for ever and ever and no rest day or night.
Fulfillment: Awaited as a final judgment on beast-worshippers, distinct from the general judgment of the dead; the nature and duration of the torment are debated among interpreters, so the entry states the prediction's terms without settling that debate.

Prophecy: The Harvest of the Earth and the Winepress of Wrath
ProphecySummary: One like the Son of man on a white cloud reaps the harvest of the earth with a sharp sickle when it is ripe, and then an angel gathers the clusters of the vine of the earth and casts them into the great winepress of God's wrath, which is trodden outside the city until blood comes out of the winepress, even to the horses' bridles, for sixteen hundred furlongs.
Fulfillment: Debated: the harvest is read by some as the gathering of the righteous and by others as judgment itself, while the winepress is a judgment image; both acts are presented as one end-time reaping sequence whose timing and referents are disputed.

Prophecy: The Gathering of the Kings at Armageddon
ProphecySummary: The river Euphrates is dried up so that the way of the kings of the east may be prepared, and three unclean spirits like frogs from the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet go out working miracles to gather the kings of the earth and of the whole world to the battle of the great day of God Almighty, at a place called in Hebrew Armageddon.
Fulfillment: Debated: whether this is a literal future battle at a literal site, a symbolic gathering of world powers against God, or an event already foreshadowed in history is disputed; the gathering itself is stated as a future confrontation, not dated.

Prophecy: The Beast and the False Prophet Cast into the Lake of Fire
ProphecySummary: The beast and the kings of the earth with their armies gather to make war against him who sits on the white horse and his army; the beast is taken, and with him the false prophet who worked miracles before him and deceived those who received the mark and worshipped the image, and both are cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone, while the remnant are slain by the sword from the rider's mouth.
Fulfillment: Awaited as the end of the beast's reign: the identities of the beast and false prophet are debated, but their capture and casting into the lake of fire are presented as a future act of the returning King, after which the devil's own casting follows in the thousand-years sequence.

Prophecy: The New Jerusalem Descending from Heaven
ProphecySummary: The holy city, new Jerusalem, descends out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband, with a great high wall and twelve gates of pearl bearing the names of Israel's twelve tribes, twelve foundations bearing the apostles' names, streets of pure gold, no temple within because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple, no need of sun or moon because God's glory lights it, gates never shut by day for there is no night there, the river of the water of life and the tree of life with leaves for the healing of the nations, no more curse, and God's servants seeing his face and reigning for ever and ever.
Fulfillment: Awaited: the city is described as descending at the consummation, after the first heaven and earth pass away; it is the dwelling of God with men promised in the new creation, not yet seen.
